notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/dgretton__pyhamilton --backend fake (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null); no hardware was attached, no hardware backend was run, native.py was never imported, and no human review or hardware test is claimed. At R2 the loader refuses an unreviewed model-written hardware backend; no other protection is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names PythonObjectDriver; this package is a direct decorated Driver over the card entry symbol pyhamilton.interface:HamiltonInterface with a native.py adapter. The upstream interface starts an OEM process and a localhost server and sends JSON command dictionaries; its aspirate and dispense take deck-object tuples and a liquid class, which a static family configuration cannot express. The card's other entry symbol ThermalCyclerProtocol exists (pyhamilton/odtc/odtc_protocol.py:4) but is not driven here.

COVERAGE: reads is_open and server_exited; actions x-cap.dgretton.initialize.v1, aspirate.v1, dispense.v1, move_plate.v1 (iSWAP by sequence), set_labware_property.v1 and shutdown_interface.v1 (safe_state=True); @estop and @reset; setup and teardown call the native start and stop. Both numeric inputs (the volume of aspirate and dispense) are Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json supplies example bounds (1 to 200 uL) only to run the suite and is not a claim about any robot. No text of the clone states a volume, flow, force or travel bound for a configured robot.

NOT COVERED: tip pickup and eject, the 96-well and 384-quadrant commands, the gripper commands, move_sequence, load_carrier and unload_carrier, set_log_dir, the ODTC ThermalCyclerProtocol and the device wrappers. The native adapter constructs a Plate96 for every labware name, so 384-well and other deck resources are not covered. The hardware path was never run. The clone ships no simulator; the fake is an in-memory stand-in for the upstream methods the driver calls, deliberately accepts commands while stopped (so the e-stop latch and reset can be exercised), and reports the requested volume rather than a measurement. The upstream simulating flag only logs and does not emulate the robot. The fake defines only public methods that exist on HamiltonInterface (gate G7).
